key_insight: HVAF spraying can produce thick NiTi coatings that retain martensitic transformation and shape-memory functionality after annealing, overcoming a key limitation of conventional spray routes.
engineering_relevance: This enables adherent, functional NiTi surface layers for smart wear, friction, corrosion, and thermal-actuation applications on engineering components.
method: HVAF-sprayed NiTi onto mild steel using four processing parameter sets
Characterized chemical composition, porosity, microstructure, and phase transformation behavior
Tested functional response via 3-point bending, nanoindentation, and scratch experiments
evidence_signal: The coatings were 100–300 μm thick, adhered well to the substrate, and showed martensitic transformation plus thermal actuation/shape-memory response after annealing.
watch_item: As-sprayed coatings are microstructurally inhomogeneous with voids, oxides, dislocations, and internal stress, so post-spray annealing is needed and tensile strength remains limited.
paper_title: HVAF Spraying of NiTi Coatings: Microstructure, Phase Transformation and Shape Memory Behavior
